A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same graphon-mixture framework, despite the revised title and presentation. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic clustering experiments, GMAM and MGCL benchmark results, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds graphon-recovery evaluations, sensitivity experiments, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain motif-based clustering, representative-graph selection, SIGL estimation, graphon interpolation, graphon-aware edge resampling, and cluster-restricted negative sampling. The training objective remains unchanged in Algorithm 3 and the aggregate-loss equation.

E1.justification: v3 removes RDT-M5K from MGCL classification and false-negative evaluation, reducing that coverage from eight datasets to seven. The dataset remains evaluated under GMAM. The seven synthetic graphon families and GMAM benchmark coverage are retained.

E2.justification: v3 adds DisenGCN to the synthetic clustering comparison, reporting 18.0% varying-size and 19.2% fixed-size accuracy in Table 2. Table 8 also introduces an oracle single-graphon estimation comparator. The main GMAM and MGCL comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include GW loss against an oracle estimation control, ARI comparisons over 2–10 clusters, synthetic mixtures with 2–7 components, a GMAM cluster-count sweep, and separate runtime measurements for preprocessing and training. Existing training budgets, the mixup 7:1:2 split, and MGCL's 10-fold SVM evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands validation through graphon-recovery analysis, synthetic cluster-count sensitivity, mixture-complexity robustness, GMAM cluster-count ablation, and runtime analysis (Appendices A.2 and F.2–F.4). The original motif-count ablation remains, while MGCL sensitivity curves and false-negative evaluation coverage are revised.

E5.justification: Both versions retain eight-run mixup reporting, shared-seed statements, and ten-trial MGCL cluster-count experiments. The existing ± and error-bar reporting practices continue; no new confidence-interval, significance-testing, or repeated-run procedure is specified.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial recovery, ARI, sensitivity, and runtime results. Table 3 changes MGCL's COLLAB result from 72.22±0.72 to 72.28±0.63 and removes RDT-M5K; average rank changes from 1.62 across eight datasets to 1.42 across seven, not a comparable performance gain. MGCL ablation curves also change, including the PROTEINS optimum from nine clusters to six. The main GMAM accuracy table is unchanged.

T1.justification: The concentration bounds, complexity analysis, and Appendix B/C proofs are retained. However, v3's added per-anchor loss definition following Equation 12 uses log(ratio), whereas v1 Equation 16 uses negative log(ratio). This creates a localized mathematical inconsistency with v3's aggregate objective and unchanged proof.

C1.justification: The three central contributions remain. v3 adds an explicit claim to the first motif-based graphon clustering approach and narrows MGCL's headline coverage from eight benchmarks to seven. Its conclusion changes GMAM's state-of-the-art claim from seven benchmarks to six, aligning it with the retained results and original abstract.

C2.justification: v3 adds a prior-work-based stability rationale for graphon-aware augmentation and interpretations of recovery quality, runtime overhead, merging similar graphon components, and excessive clustering causing fragmentation. The existing limitation concerning sampling variance in small graphs remains.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 newly documents measured times for motif computation, clustering/graphon estimation, and training/validation. The previously disclosed hyperparameters, architectures, hardware, software versions, and data-source information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Ma et al. (2019) for DisenGCN and Ruiz et al. (2020) to motivate representation stability under graphon-based augmentation. It also strengthens novelty positioning through the explicit first-approach claim. Other reference changes largely update bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: The title and author block change, and the abstract, contribution statements, and selected explanatory and results paragraphs are rewritten. Baseline descriptions and appendix analyses are regrouped. The main section sequence and most method, algorithm, and proof text remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main-text layout and extensively reformats and relocates displays. It adds runtime and GMAM-sensitivity figures plus Tables 8–11, redraws MGCL sensitivity plots, and removes the RDT-M5K column and false-negative bars. Existing bound plots and graphon illustrations are retained but relocated and resized.

improvement.justification: The new graphon-recovery, sensitivity, and runtime evidence strengthens validation of the central mixture-estimation stage beyond v1's existing clustering and downstream results. Several benchmark-summary claims are also corrected. These benefits are tempered by reduced MGCL coverage, the new loss-sign inconsistency, and revised MGCL plots whose discussion still describes old optima, yielding a limited net improvement.
